LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 4.3.1 WORD CLASS: POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Which words show something belongs to a person? 2. Why should we use possessive forms correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: Team work as learner engages in online or offline games involving pronouns such as dice, goofy cards and

word search.

• Citizenship: Information and communication skills to compose signed songs based on the use of personal and possessive pronouns.

Values:
Responsibility: Hard work as learner use pronouns in spoken or signed and written sentences to show possession

Link to other Subjects:

The learners are able to relate the concept of pronouns to similar concepts in Kiswahili.
